I want to correct something almost everybody in this room believes. An improvement plan is not the paperwork you do before you let somebody go. If that is what it is in your organisation, then you are using it as a legal shield and your people know it. A real one has three things in it. A behaviour, described so precisely that a stranger could tell you whether it happened. A date, which is usually thirty, sixty or ninety days. And the support the company is putting in, which is the part people leave blank. If the company puts nothing in, you are not asking for a turnaround, you are asking for a miracle. And one more thing. If this is the first the person is hearing about it, the plan is not the problem. The eleven months of silence before it are the problem.

The feedback that changed how I work was four sentences long and my director gave it standing up, on a Tuesday, in a corridor. She said, you answer every question with a longer question. People leave your meetings without a decision and they think it is their fault. If you gave one answer before you asked anything back, half of your meetings would be shorter. And then she said, that is it, go. What made it land was not the corridor and it was not the four sentences. It was that she described something I do, not something I am. She did not say I was indecisive. She said I answer questions with questions, and I could check that. I went back through my last five meetings and she was right every time.
